method: reference-locked multi-view ImageGen design-source pack followed by authored metric Blender geometry and custom PBR extraction
binding_identity: A two-storey French Third Republic municipal school whose long symmetrical red-brick classroom wings, cream limestone dressings, three recessed civic entrances, tall arched occupied windows, slate hips, chimney pairs and central clock pavilion read as one sober Jules Ferry-era public monument.

research.role: Regional heritage inventory precedent for classical symmetry, brick elevation, central stair/clock element and school planning.
City of Paris heritage record describing a representative 1880 Jules Ferry school, its monumental civic intent, meuliere base, brick effects and parallel classroom blocks.
French Ministry of Culture record for classroom-bay cadence, pressed brick arches and decorative frieze/crowning.
Departmental heritage precedent for a symmetrical Third Republic school with central clock, civic inscription, brick banding and meuliere base.
Freely viewable real-building precedent for central clock pediment, civic inscription hierarchy and brick/stone material balance.

assets.purpose: canonical street identity and proportion goalpost
assets.prompt: Create a premium photorealistic architectural reference photograph, 3:2 landscape, of one complete French Third Republic municipal primary school circa 1885–1905. This is a canonical identity goalpost for a 3D model, not an illustration. Camera is at human eye level across a quiet street, centered with only restrained three-quarter perspective so the entire 40-metre-wide front facade and a little of the right return are legible. The building is a dignified low two-storey horizontal school, approximately 40 m wide by 15 m deep, rigorously symmetrical: a slightly projecting three-bay central pavilion rises above two long classroom wings, and the center terminates in a small square clock/bell pavilion with a real round clock beneath a steep grey slate hipped cap. Red-brown pressed brick in fine Flemish bond forms the wall fields. Cream limestone is physically modeled as a rough meuliere/stone plinth, corner quoins, continuous string courses, arched window surrounds, keystones, sills, central entrance portal, and a rectangular carved civic inscription panel that is present but contains no legible lettering. Each wing has a recessed arched pupil entrance near the central pavilion, visually paired as historic separate entrances, plus a larger central administration entrance. Tall classroom windows are deeply recessed, vertically proportioned, and terminate in segmental or semicircular brick-and-stone arches; each has dark green painted timber frames, real divided low-reflectance glass, visible jamb depth, shadowed occupied interiors, pale curtains, and occasional warm pendant lights—never flat black rectangles. The upper floor window rhythm is regular and educational rather than residential. Include projecting brick pilasters, decorative brick corbel-table cornice, limestone dentils, zinc gutters and downpipes, several brick chimney clusters, a few small zinc dormers, and subtle slate variation. A low dark-green cast-iron fence on a meuliere curb encloses a shallow paved school forecourt with two mature plane trees placed away from the facade. Materials must read as real aged brick, porous cream stone, rough meuliere, matte natural slate, zinc and glass, with restrained weathering. Bright overcast French daylight, neutral white balance, realistic lens and shadows, high-detail professional heritage-architecture photography. No people in front of key facade details, no cars, no fantasy, no château, no church, no modern glass curtain wall, no oversized tower, no cartoon, no painterly styling, no fake textual signs or watermark.

Using the attached canonical French Third Republic school as the binding design source, create a render-locked rectified architectural front elevation image of exactly the same building and material system. Orthographic front view, zero perspective, complete facade centered and not cropped, 3:2 landscape, plain pale neutral background and a narrow neutral ground strip. Preserve the identity precisely: 40 m wide, two full occupied floors, symmetrical central three-bay pavilion projecting slightly, long balanced classroom wings, central square clock pavilion with round clock and steep slate hipped cap, four chimney stacks total, small zinc dormers, dark grey natural-slate hipped roofs, red-brown Flemish-bond brick wall fields, cream limestone quoins/string courses/deep arched window surrounds/keystones/sills/cornice/dentils, rough meuliere plinth, dark green timber frames and doors, zinc gutters and downpipes. Show three distinct real recessed entrances: one centered administration entrance and paired arched pupil entrances flanking the central pavilion, integrated into the masonry rather than applied. Include a blank carved civic inscription panel above the center, with no legible writing. Tall classroom windows must have consistent dimensional rhythm, genuinely recessed jambs, dark-green frame thickness, divided glass panes, varied low-E sky reflections, pale curtains and softly occupied interior depth—never black or flat. Include no trees, fence, people, vehicles, street furniture, cast shadows across the facade, labels, dimensions, watermark, text, fantasy, château styling, or modern glazing. This must look like a clean high-resolution heritage survey elevation rendered with physically accurate aged brick, porous limestone, rough stone base, slate, zinc, painted timber and glass—not a drawing or cartoon.

assets.purpose: roof topology and complete massing registration
assets.prompt: Create a premium photorealistic oblique aerial reference of exactly the same French Third Republic municipal school shown in the attached street goalpost and rectified elevation. This is the binding roof-and-massing source for a metric 3D model. Camera about 20 metres high over the front-left corner, 3:2 landscape, entire freestanding 40 m by 15 m building visible and centered, no cropping. Preserve the exact two-storey symmetrical brick-and-limestone composition and central raised three-bay pavilion. The roof must be architecturally coherent and buildable: two long grey natural-slate hipped wing roofs meeting a slightly taller central hipped pavilion; a small square clock/bell tower centered on the ridge with a steep four-sided slate cap and zinc finial; four paired red-brick chimney stacks near the wing ends; four small zinc-framed dormers aligned to front classrooms; real zinc ridges, hips, valleys, flashings, gutters and dark downpipes. Show subtle individual slate courses and restrained weathering, not a smooth grey slab. The facade below retains red-brown Flemish-bond brick, cream limestone quoins/string courses/arched surrounds, rough meuliere base, deeply recessed dark-green divided windows and three arched entrance portals. The rear must be legible as a working school: regular tall classroom windows, a centered shallow rear stair pavilion, two simple dark-green service doors, zinc canopy, and a paved fenced schoolyard, while keeping the same material language. Include only a minimal neutral site apron and a few plane-tree crowns at the perimeter without blocking the building. Bright overcast daylight, neutral white balance, physically accurate material response, realistic heritage architectural photography. No city skyline, no cars, no crowd, no fantasy, no church or château, no mansard roof, no flat roof, no modern additions, no text, no watermark, no cartoon or miniature effect.

assets.purpose: rear schoolyard elevation and service logic registration
assets.prompt: Create a render-locked rectified architectural REAR elevation of exactly the same French Third Republic municipal school shown in the attached goalpost and aerial. Orthographic rear view, zero perspective, complete 40 m facade centered and not cropped, 3:2 landscape, plain pale neutral background and narrow neutral schoolyard ground strip. Maintain the same two-storey red-brown Flemish-bond brick and cream-limestone construction, rough meuliere plinth, symmetrical long wings, slate hipped roof, four chimney stacks, four dormers, and centered clock pavilion visible above the ridge. The rear is functional but carefully composed: a shallow three-bay central stair pavilion projects 0.8 m; its center has a vertically stacked pair of tall divided stair windows with genuine recessed jambs and a smaller fanlight at grade. On each classroom wing place a regular rhythm of four tall arched classroom windows per floor, with real cream limestone surrounds, keystones and sills. Add two dark-green timber service doors at ground floor, one on each side of the stair pavilion, each under a narrow zinc-and-iron canopy. Windows use dark-green painted timber frames, divided low-E glass, pale curtains and softly occupied classroom depth, never black flat panes. Continue the stone string courses, brick pilasters, corbel cornice, zinc gutters/downpipes, slate courses and restrained weathering around the rear. A dark-green iron fence and simple paved schoolyard may be shown only as a narrow bottom band; no trees or equipment may obscure the facade. Bright overcast neutral daylight, physically accurate heritage materials, premium survey-render realism. No front entrances, no ornate front inscription panel, no people, cars, playground clutter, modern additions, external fire stairs, text, labels, watermark, cartoon, drawing, fantasy, church or château.

assets.purpose: custom brick, limestone, meuliere and slate skin source
assets.prompt: Create a high-resolution square photogrammetry-style MATERIAL SOURCE sheet for the exact masonry palette of the attached French Third Republic school. Orthographic, evenly lit, shadow-neutral, no perspective and no labels. Arrange four large contiguous clean sample quadrants with straight boundaries: (1) aged red-brown pressed brick in accurate small Flemish bond with subtle brick-to-brick variation, thin warm-grey lime mortar, crisp but not exaggerated recessed joints; (2) porous warm cream limestone ashlar with restrained fine fossil/grain detail and lightly weathered edges; (3) rustic tan-grey meuliere rubble stone with irregular rounded aggregate and natural mortar; (4) dark grey natural slate roof courses with thin staggered rectangular slates, slight thickness and restrained blue-grey variation. The samples must tile cleanly and have diffuse albedo-style illumination suitable for deriving PBR albedo, roughness, normal, AO and depth maps. Real construction material photography, neutral white balance, maximum micro-detail. No windows, doors, building perspective, cast shadows, moss, stains, dramatic lighting, text, numbers, borders, watermark, cartoon, CGI gloss, or random props.

assets.purpose: physical glazing, opening depth and occupied-room registration
assets.prompt: Create a high-resolution square WINDOW AND ENTRY DEPTH SOURCE sheet for the exact French Third Republic school in the attached elevation. Orthographic close-up, evenly lit, physically realistic, no labels. Arrange four large clean reference quadrants: top-left a tall segmental-arched classroom window seen straight-on with full cream limestone surround, keystone, sill and visibly deep brick jamb; dark-green painted timber outer frame, six-over-six divided panes, clear low-E glass with soft pale-sky reflection, curtains and a convincing occupied classroom 0.5–1.0 m behind the pane with desks/shelves/pendant light only as subdued depth cues. Top-right a semicircular arched pupil entrance with cream stone archivolt, recessed dark-green timber double doors, fanlight glazing, threshold and three shallow stone steps, showing real wall thickness. Bottom-left a close material-detail view of the window frame and operable lower casement, showing timber profiles, mullions, putty lines, glass thickness, subtle smudging and interior curtain offset. Bottom-right a zinc-and-wrought-iron service-door canopy with brackets, gutter edge, downpipe connection, dark-green door and adjacent brick/limestone junction. Every opening must be physically recessed, dimensionally coherent and suitable as a design source for modeled frames, glass cavities and occupied interiors. Neutral overcast daylight, restrained reflections, heritage-building photography, maximum material detail. No flat black panes, no mirror chrome, no modern aluminum storefront, no people, no text, numbers, signs, watermark, dramatic shadows, collage borders, cartoon or illustration.

assets.purpose: single continuous low-contrast classroom plate behind separate physical glazing
assets.prompt: Create a single seamless square OCCUPIED CLASSROOM DEPTH PLATE for the French Third Republic school shown in the references. This is not a collage and contains no exterior window frame or glass. Camera is perfectly straight-on from just outside one opening, looking 0.8–1.2 metres into a softly occupied late-19th-century classroom. Fill the entire square with one continuous low-contrast interior: warm plaster ceiling and walls, dark timber wainscot, two rows of simple wood desks, a muted chalkboard, shallow book shelves, pale linen curtains only at the far left and right edges, and two small warm pendant lamps. Keep the central field calm and dark enough to sit behind separate low-E glass; details should be readable as depth but never become a repeating high-contrast pattern. Neutral overcast daylight enters from the camera side, mixed with restrained warm practical light. Shadow-neutral, realistic heritage interior photography, no people, no exterior masonry, no window sash, no mullions, no reflections, no multiple panels, no collage borders, no text, no signs, no watermark, no cartoon, no dramatic perspective or bright white highlights.

assets.purpose: clock pavilion, roof junction, cornice and chimney geometry source
assets.prompt: Create a high-resolution square ARCHITECTURAL DETAIL SOURCE sheet for the same French Third Republic school. Four clean, nearly orthographic quadrants with neutral overcast light and no labels: top-left the central square clock pavilion straight-on, with dark slate-clad or dark-painted face field, a real round cream clock bezel, black Roman-style tick geometry without legible words, cream limestone corner pilasters, projecting cornice, steep slate pyramidal cap, zinc hips and finial; top-right the junction between central pavilion and long slate hipped wing roof, showing stepped limestone shoulders, zinc valley/flashings, slate courses, gutter and downpipe logic; bottom-left a close straight-on sample of the brick corbel-table cornice and cream limestone dentil/eaves course, physically projecting with real shadows; bottom-right a paired red-brick chimney cluster on the slate roof, showing corbelled brick caps, terracotta pots, lead/zinc flashing and individual slate courses. Maintain exactly the red-brown brick, warm cream limestone, grey natural slate and zinc palette. Photoreal heritage construction documentation, maximum geometric and material clarity, usable to model real depth. No full building, no people, no text or labels, no watermark, no fantasy ornament, no church steeple, no cartoon, no dramatic lighting.
